newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank sells 202 mln kuna bills.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank sells 202 mln kuna bills.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 202 million kuna in its liquidity bills at an auction on Wednesday and banking investors ventured into 182-day paper for the first time in months.
Volume was stronger after being subdued for weeks due to liquidity strains, with fresh investment totalling 42 million kuna while the rest were renewed subscriptions, an official told Reuters.
"Banks generally have more money," the official added.
They bought two million kuna worth of the central bank's longest maturity at 9.5 percent, down from 17 percent last November when it was last issued.
The issued rates for 35- and 91-day bills were unchanged at 7.0 and 8.5 percent, respectively. Full results are available on page NBHT.
As banks' total balances rose, Monday's reserve payment drained 3.48 billion kuna from the system or 55 million more than a fortnight ago. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
